### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/driver-sql`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **176** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b41c5a46ba3de65f602412554577e66c7a7720e1` — the merge of head `e689bd7db84b327b38a84f80d1c913899b1a0ff2` into base `631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b41c5a46ba3de65f602412554577e66c7a7720e1 && git checkout b41c5a46ba3de65f602412554577e66c7a7720e1
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6 e689bd7db84b327b38a84f80d1c913899b1a0ff2 && git checkout -B drift-repro 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6 && git merge --no-ff e689bd7db84b327b38a84f80d1c913899b1a0ff2

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 631d77f3021ca00e36a3cb51e19a4d8ee361fdc6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7148349e5a6927e129b1b8adb485e5d6480ea309`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts, packages/objectql/src/engine.ts, packages/objectql/src/lock-rows-refusal-error.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver-crud.ts, packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #34373 body and all 8 comments (triage, ruling 6919195250, four claims, the needs_seat report with routes A/B/C, the done report), PR #34517 body, file list and the net diff against the merge base with main, and the check-runs on the head. Nothing was built or run.

Check-runs on the head: 67 runs. Every completed run concluded success or skipped; none failed. Pending at the time of reading: `Test UI (10/16)` (in progress, no verdict; the diff holds no UI file). `Test Core` (the aggregate) and all eight Test Core shards, the three Type Check runs, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` and the PR-body guards are success. ⚠️ `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)` is skipped on a pull request by its own `if:` (full battery only), so no check-run on this head executed the live PostgreSQL or MySQL row-lock cells of `sql-driver-34373-lock-rows.test.ts`: on this head they are ordinary skips. The live PostgreSQL reading is the dev's own local one (PR body, ablation A1); the MySQL cell has been run by nobody yet and first runs on main's full battery. The PR body sentence "CI's Temporal Conformance runs the MySQL cell" is true of main, not of this head.

Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies:

- `DriverOptionsSchema` gains optional boolean `lockRows`. A widening: every bag that parsed still parses. Right.
- `DriverCapabilitiesSchema` gains optional boolean `lockRows`, absence meaning false. A widening, on the `aggregationFilter` precedent (one optional bit landed with its engine reader). Right. The audited shape pin moves to 6 live bits + 31 tombstones and `authorable-surface/data.json` gains both keys, matching.
- Because `declaredDriverOptionKeys()` reads the schema shape, `lockRows` now crosses the engine to driver hop from every bag `buildDriverOptions` is given. The diff answers that in the same function: 501 `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` when the object's driver lacks the bit, 428 `PRECONDITION_REQUIRED` when no transaction reaches it. Right, and necessary: without the guard the new key would be a silently ignored option on every non-declaring driver reached through the engine.
- One input that used to succeed now refuses: a bag with no closed option set (an insert's options) carrying `lockRows: true`. Before this diff the key was undeclared and dropped at the hop without a sound; now it answers 501 or 428. This is a refusal of a key that had no meaning and no caller before this PR (no sender in the tree; read by grep at head), not the narrowing of a published accept set. Judged right, and not a `(narrowing)` arm.
- The find, findOne, delete, update, count and aggregate verbs keep refusing `lockRows` at their closed option sets (unchanged, pinned for find and delete). Right: the engine's one sender stays its own.
- `SqlDriver.supports.lockRows: true` on every dialect, and `find()` / `findOne()` gain a 428 refusal for `lockRows` with no transaction. New behaviour on a new key only. Right. `SqliteWasmDriver` inherits both with no override (knex compiles nothing for SQLite; one connection).
- Engine behaviour: the cascade arm's matched-row read is a locking read when the unit has a handle and the driver declares the bit. No outcome changes without a concurrent writer; rows deleted are still exactly the rows walked (the #26871 / #27004 invariant kept). Right.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/34373-predicate-delete-lock-rows.md`: `@objectstack/spec` minor, `@objectstack/objectql` patch, `@objectstack/driver-sql` patch. This is the level the precedent changeset for `aggregationFilter` (#33698) took for the same shape of change, and minor is right for two optional additive keys on published schemas. All three packages sit in the one fixed version group, so the release bump is the group's minor either way. `Check Changeset` is success.

`Clause-②: yes (widening: DriverOptions.lockRows and DriverCapabilities.lockRows)` is present and identical on the PR body and in the changeset, and it is true of the diff: both spec edits widen, nothing published is narrowed. `Metadata-protocol: added` matches the two new authorable-surface entries. No `!` is owed and none is claimed.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:

- `packages/objectql/src/engine-driver-options.ts` edited though the last claim's file surface names only the `engine.ts` host line and the new error file. Accepted: `buildDriverOptions` lives there, the claim describes exactly this refusal seam, and the hunk is the guard and nothing else.
- Ablations A1 to A4 run with vitest directly, outside `os-verify-lock`. A process deviation with no effect on the contract; accepted.
- First gate pass before the last commit, re-run in full at this head. Accepted; the recorded pass is the head's.
- Local heap flag for `check:test-typecheck`. Environmental; the CI type-check runs are success without it.

Open questions, each answered:

- Q1, route to contract review or land without: answered by this record.
- Q2, should the memory, MongoDB and OData drivers refuse 501 when called DIRECTLY with `lockRows`: no, not in this card (option A). Judged against declared ⇒ enforced: the option's TSDoc says "A driver honours it only when it declares `DriverCapabilities.lockRows`", and every refusal it promises is scoped to the engine ("its read and delete verbs do not take the key", "refused there", at the engine to driver hop). The capability's TSDoc says the same from the other side ("an option a driver silently ignores is a lock the engine believes it holds and does not. The bit is the driver's promise"). So the contract text as written does NOT promise more than the code enforces: the enforcement point it names is the capability bit plus the engine's guard, and both exist and are pinned (501 and 428 with code and status). What the text leaves unsaid, rather than over-promised, is the plain consequence for a direct caller: a non-declaring driver ignores the key, so a direct caller must read `supports.lockRows` first. That is nit N1 below. Option B (a 501 in each driver) is a sound follow-up if a direct driver caller that sends the key ever exists; none does in the tree at this head.
- Q3, Turso remote inherits the bit, and MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle are not measured live: accept for this card (option A), with two follow-ups named in ④ (N2, N3). Through the engine both are safe: the engine sends the key only with an open handle that covers the object's driver, and a caller's own `lockRows` on a transport with no transaction answers 428 at the hop. See ① for what CI did and did not measure on this head.

SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no new in-app join. The id read followed by `id $in` batches is the arm's existing shape, with its reason on the tree (#26871, #27004: the walk's own writes can move a row into or out of the predicate, so the rows deleted must be the rows walked). This diff adds a lock to that existing read and pushes it down as the dialect's own locking read. No finding.

Open PR #34530 (card #33697) also edits `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`: it adds the capability bit `zonedDateBucketing`, read by `engine.aggregate`. The two edits do not collide in meaning: different bits, different verbs (`aggregate()` against `find()`), different engine readers, and neither changes what the other's bit promises. They do collide in text and in one counted fact: both append after `aggregationFilter` in the schema, the header bullet list, the `SqlDriver.supports` literal, `LIVE_BITS` and the three generated `driver*.mdx` tables, and BOTH rename the audited-shape pin to "6 live bits + 31 tombstones" and call their bit "the sixth". Whichever lands second must merge main, make that 7 live bits (title and comments; the identical title line can merge textually clean and stay wrong), and regenerate. The claim already records that the area serialises the landing.

Not in the diff, recorded for the seat: on PostgreSQL a locking read needs UPDATE privilege on the table in addition to SELECT (PostgreSQL's documented rule; not measured here). A platform-owned table is unaffected. A federated object whose remote role holds DELETE without UPDATE, and which delete-family lookups reference, would have its predicate delete refused by the database where it ran before. Rare and loud; worth one line in a follow-up card, not a finding on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts`, against ruling route B on the card (lock the matched rows inside the unit of work, then keep the delete by id; a driver option or capability; drivers without row locks keep the window and say so) and against its first consumer, the cascade arm of `runPredicateDelete`:

- The schema implements route B as ruled, with the names the seat ruled (claim 6931526435). Option and bit are both optional booleans; absence of the bit is false. Holds.
- The option's TSDoc, sentence by sentence: "only with `transaction` set" is enforced twice (428 at the hop, 428 in `lockRowsIfAsked`); "honours it only when it declares the bit" is enforced by the 501 at the hop; "read and delete verbs do not take the key" is the closed option sets, pinned; "the engine's one sender" is true of the tree (one `lockRows: true` literal in `packages/objectql/src`). Holds.
- The bit's TSDoc: the promise ("the writer waits ... or one of the two fails loudly; a writer's commit is never followed by a successful write of the transaction over the changed row") is the right strength. It is what every dialect can keep, it covers a deadlock abort, and it is exactly what the card's guard needs. `FOR UPDATE` is the right lock strength for rows about to be deleted. The SQLite paragraph matches the two committed two-connection pins (WAL: the transaction's delete fails `SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT`; rollback journal: the writer fails `SQLITE_BUSY`). "The memory, MongoDB and OData drivers keep that window" states the residue the ruling required be stated. Holds.
- Tried to break it: (1) a predicate that compiles to a join, where PostgreSQL refuses a lock on the nullable side: `findRows` builds no join, and composed scope leaves compile to subqueries, which lock only the outer rows. (2) DISTINCT or GROUP BY under the lock: not on the `find` path. (3) The retry ladder dropping the lock: every rung is rebuilt by `buildBase`, which re-applies it. (4) The 428 being swallowed into a statement fault: it is thrown while building, outside the try. (5) The engine's own send escaping its guard: it checks the handle and the bit itself, and the handle in `writeOptions` is only ever one `transactionCoversDriverFor` admitted. (6) A row moved INTO the predicate after the read: not walked, not deleted, as before. None broke.
- Considered and accepted as inside the stated promise: locking the root first can deadlock against a writer that holds a child row and then writes the parent (a roll-up recompute). The database aborts one side loudly; "or one of the two fails" covers it.

Implementing files:

- `engine-delete-and-aggregate.ts`: agrees with the contract. The lock rides the matched-row read only; the walk and the by-id deletes keep `writeOptions`. The comment's "no open transaction (the `'split'` plan ...)" is slightly narrower than the code, which also locks under a `'split'` plan when an ambient handle covers the root's driver; the code is the safer of the two.
- `engine-driver-options.ts`, `engine.ts`, `lock-rows-refusal-error.ts`: agree. Both codes exist in `StandardErrorCode` with those statuses; the error carries `code`, `status` and `httpStatus`; refusal happens before any driver call (pinned: nothing written).
- `sql-driver-crud.ts`, `sql-driver.ts`: agree. `find()` and `findOne()` both pass through `findRows`, so both honour the key, as the option's TSDoc says.

N1 (nit) — the option's TSDoc never says outright that a driver WITHOUT the bit ignores the key on a direct call, so a direct caller must read `supports.lockRows` first. The text does not claim otherwise; one sentence would close the question the dev raised. Left as an accepted deviation on this head (a fix moves the head); fold it into the follow-up below.

N2 (nit) — the bit's TSDoc states the MySQL and SQL Server behaviour as fact and the driver declares the bit on every dialect, Oracle included, while only PostgreSQL and SQLite are measured (the `aggregationFilter` precedent names its measured dialects). On SQL Server and Oracle the lock is knex's compile, unread against a server; on Oracle a `findOne()` with `lockRows` (a row limit under a locking read) is likely refused by the database. Both failures would be loud, and the engine's one sender uses neither a limit nor `findOne`. Follow-up card: measure the MySQL, SQL Server and Oracle cells and name the measured dialects in the TSDoc.

N3 (nit) — `TursoDriver` (outside this repository) inherits `lockRows: true` while its remote transport carries no transaction. The engine never sends it the key, and a caller's own request answers 428 at the hop, so nothing is wrong through the engine. By the precedent the same literal's comments set for `transactionsUnsupported` and `aggregationFilter` (a subclass whose transport cannot do it spreads the baseline and turns the bit off), the remote mode should declare `lockRows: false`. Follow-up card in the driver's own repository.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e689bd7db84b327b38a84f80d1c913899b1a0ff2`
